title: NHC's 2025 season verification: Google DeepMind ensemble mean outperformed official short-range Atlantic track forecasts in NHC's first operational use of AI models
summary: NHC's 2025 verification: Google DeepMind ensemble mean beat official Atlantic track forecasts at 12–72 h; first AI models in NHC operations.
account: The National Hurricane Center's Forecast Verification Report for the 2025 season is dated 30 March 2026. It states that 2025 marked the first time NHC incorporated AI-based models into real-time operations. In the Atlantic track comparison, the Google DeepMind ensemble mean (GDMI) slightly outperformed the official forecast at lead times from 12 to 72 h. Official forecasts outperformed the consensus aids TVCA, HCCA and FSSE. In the eastern North Pacific, GDMI performed considerably better than every other individual model. It beat the official forecast and all consensus aids at 48–120 h. For intensity it was the top individual model from 12 to 48 h. GDMI was not available early in the season, so the first storms are excluded from these comparisons.
purpose: Experimental AI tropical cyclone forecast model providing ensemble track and intensity guidance to NHC forecasters.
system: Google DeepMind AI hurricane forecast model, ensemble mean designated GDMI in NHC guidance

headline: DeepMind's GDMI beats NHC Atlantic track forecasts at 12–72 h
metric: beat official Atlantic track forecasts at 12–72 h

comparator.against: the NHC official track forecast (OFCL) in the 2025 Atlantic homogeneous model comparison
comparator.after: GDMI errors of 19.6, 26.4, 34.8, 41.4, 50.8 and 66.5 n mi at the same lead times
comparator.quote: The official forecasts were highly skillful, even outperforming the typically reliable consensus aids TVCA, HCCA, and FSSE. However, there was one model, the Google DeepMind ensemble mean (GDMI), that slightly outperformed NHC at the shorter lead times from 12 to 72 h.
